about: Pad (your phone as a remote for your call) - shared test vectors for the pure rules, byte-identical in the web repo (src/features/calls/pad/vectors.json) and the desktop repo (crates/app/src/testvectors/pad.json); the contract is docs/PAD.md in both. trust: rules 1-4 on facts (each overrides defaults.receiverFacts); every failure is a silent drop with that reason, run through checkTrust, checkPadMessage (an open) and acceptState. cmds: one command after an implicit open (sid PhoneSession0001, seq 1, ts 1000, now 1000, want [talk], default facts and ctx); the case's msg is merged over the envelope {v:1, sid, seq:2, ts:1500, room, gen:g1}, `drop` removes keys, `raw` replaces the content, `type` the event type, `now` defaults to 1500. sessions: steps against one receiver table; a step's msg is merged over {v:1, sid, ts:<now>, room, gen:g1}; `repeat` runs it n times with seq+1 each time; `do` steps: refuse / clearRefused / clear / sweep (expect.sids = the sids returned) and pushed / pushWait. ctx and facts merge recursively (objects merge, arrays and scalars replace) over defaults, then the scenario's, then the step's. expect on a message: ok, why, reason, reply, run always; evicted (default []); cmd and live (the live sids after the step) when present. state: buildState input -> exact output + its UTF-8 JSON size, or (generated inputs: genPeople {n, len} -> @p<i>[x...]:example.org; genRecent {n, nameLen, urlLen}) a summary. accept: steps against one controller session {sid PhoneSession0001, device PCDEVICE, lastRseq 0}; msg merges over defaults.state. targets: padTargets(me, myDevice, now, selfVerified, trusted, events) with the defaults below. rate: RateBucket.hit, n times each. stale: staleCheck(offset, ts, now); openStale: openStale(ts, now). why: whyText(code, device, op).

trust.name: plaintext from another user: not-olm first
another user (Olm sender = event sender = someone else)
Olm sender is someone else, the event claims me
Olm sender is me, the event claims someone else
Curve25519 key does not match the device record
sender key bound to no known device
own device with a mismatched key: unbound first
peer signed by the listed self-signing key but not cross-signing trusted
unverified self and untrusted peer: self first
another user who is also untrusted: other-user first

an unknown extra field is ignored

the sid of another of my devices' session -> no-session
ping with an old gen is fine (a session outlives a call switch)
ping while the receiver is not in a call
sound.play a url the receiver does not have -> unknown-sound
sound.play url not a string -> bad
sound.play url of 2049 code points -> bad
sound.play url of exactly 2048 code points is well-formed (unknown here)
sound.play with the soundboard off for my role -> off-role
sound.play while not in a call -> not-in-call
sound.play with an old gen -> other-call

mic muted:true while muted -> nothing to change
mic muted:false while unmuted -> nothing to change
mute while server-muted is allowed (muting always is)
deafen on while deafened -> nothing to change
brb off while not away -> nothing to change
vol: a live slider push (no reply)
vol: level "NaN" (NaN itself is not JSON) -> bad
vol: someone not in the call -> not-here
vol: user without a server -> bad
vol: user with a space -> bad
vol: neither level nor muted -> bad

vol: live with muted -> bad, no reply (it says it is a live push)
vol: live false is the release
vol: a live push for someone not here -> not-here, no reply
vol: a live push in another call -> other-call, no reply
vol: a live push with an unknown sid -> no-session, no reply

vol: a live push with v "1" -> bad, no reply
vol: a malformed live push -> bad, no reply

a command from another user is dropped silently
a command from an untrusted device of mine is dropped silently

sessions.name: spent sids are never forgotten early: with 64 spent + live, a new open waits (busy) until the oldest expires
rate buckets: a 17th device gets one only when a bucket has been idle for 2 s (then it is full anyway)
open -> a session (re: 1, nothing to run)
open without want: no talking rings asked for
open: want with a non-string -> bad
open: want not an array -> bad
open: an unknown want is ignored
open: gen is not read
open refused: Pad is off -> off, no session
open refused: not in a call
open for another room -> other-call
open v 2 -> version
open: 5 min off the receiver's clock is fine, more is stale
seq: duplicate and older are dropped silently, gaps are fine
a refused command uses up its seq (the retry is a new command)
a malformed command does not use up its seq
re-opening a live session never widens the clock offset (a held re-open)
re-opening after the controller's clock jumped forward tightens the offset
a closed session's open can't be replayed, and its sid is never reused
a replaced sid stays spent
a lapsed sid is spent at once and forgotten 10 min after it left the table
a refused device's sids stay spent after the refusal ends
Pad off and on again: the old sessions don't come back
a re-open of my sid from another device -> no-session (mine stays)
a session belongs to the device that opened it
lease: 45 s after the last accepted command
a dropped duplicate does not renew the lease
a fifth controller device evicts the oldest session (replaced)
one session per controller device: its new open replaces the older one
lapsed sessions do not count toward the four
stale maths: 8.000 s is fine, 8.001 s is stale
stale maths with the controller's clock 3 min ahead
a stale command still uses up its seq (and renews the lease)
rate: a burst of 16, then one busy per second, the rest dropped
rate: a live push over budget is not answered (busy still counts)
a live push from a refused device -> closed, not answered
rate: the budget is per controller device
rate: untrusted messages never touch the budget
x on the receiver: that device is refused for the rest of this call
close ends the session
the receiver switched calls: other-call for the old one, the session lives on
set-idempotence: mute twice is one change
Pad switched off: every session ends
sweep forgets lapsed sessions
push pacing: 4/s, talking-only 2/s, none while vis:false
push pacing: no talking-only pushes unless asked for, never pushed = now

sounds.name: the same url in its own room
a room without a sound list: favourites still count
a room without a sound list: no room sound
a room id that looks like a prototype key

state.name: not in a call: call null
a call: only non-default volumes, the muted categories, empty vol / mute left out
volumes: rounded to 0.01 and clamped to 0-2; a value that rounds to 1 is the default
people: invalid ids skipped, each person once (first wins)
recent: 8 at most, empty or over-long urls skipped, names cut to 64 and emoji to 16 code points
me: no sound -> null, an unknown mic -> on, a non-boolean gate -> not allowed, the hint cut to 200
me: an over-long sound url -> null; server and ptt pass
envelope numbers that are not unsigned integers -> 0, a non-string why -> ""
ids that aren't ids are sent as "" (the controller then drops the state)
the worst case besides people and recent (control characters in the sound url and hint) still fits
64 people at most, the rest counted in more
under 16 KiB with long names and urls: recent entries go first
under 16 KiB with 64 long ids: all recent, then people from the end (counted in more)

a refusal ack is a valid state
from another device of mine -> other-device
a command type at the controller -> wrong-type
a person with a bad id -> bad
me.mic not in the enum -> bad
a volume key that is not a category -> bad
mute with an unknown category -> bad
a playing sound with an empty url -> bad

targets.name: none: nobody is in the call
one: my PC is in the call
two: the newest membership first
the same created_ts: by device id
no pad1 cap (an older Tin Hat, or Pad off there) -> version
no Tin Hat marker at all (another client) -> version
caps not an array -> version
a device that is not cross-signing trusted -> untrusted
untrusted comes before version
this device is not verified -> unverified (before everything else)
an expired membership is not a target
expiry is inclusive: created + expires = now still counts
legacy array form, the marker on the entry
legacy array form, the marker on the outer content
legacy array form under another key is not mine
this device's own membership is never a target
someone else's device is never a target
not well-formed (no call_id) -> not a target
not well-formed (expires 0, still live by the clock) -> not a target
another application -> not a target
a state key naming another device -> not a target
the older state-key spelling is mine too
a tombstone (empty content) -> not a target
no created_ts: the event's origin_server_ts
mixed: newest first whatever the status (the default is the first ready one)
the same created_ts: device ids in code-point order (not UTF-16 order)
a malformed entry doesn't hide a well-formed one of the same device
one device twice: the first one counts

rate.name: a full bucket allows a burst of 16
busy at most once per second
a clock that goes back refills nothing

stale.name: a timestamp from the future is never stale
